minutes.headline: Select Board put three special town meeting articles on the warrant and held the APDC bylaw change for rework.
minutes.summary: The board reviewed special town meeting warrant articles with sponsors: firefighter credible service, motel special permit, Marshall Park engineering, and the APDC bylaw. It voted to include the first three. The APDC article drew sharp disagreement and was held for revision. The board also began reviewing ARPA requests, renewed a bond anticipation note, adopted a 300th anniversary committee charge and ratified a DPW hire.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to put the firefighter credible service article on the special town meeting warrant, unanimously.
It also voted to include the planning board's motel article and the Marshall Park engineering article; its recommendation on the motel article was put off to October 18.
The APDC bylaw article drew sharp disagreement and was held; APDC is to return October 11 or 18 with revisions.
The board renewed the bond anticipation note for the property and ladder truck at a higher rate, and early payoff in FY24 may be considered.
The board began reviewing ARPA requests, which exceed the available funds, and made no ARPA decision before the special town meeting.

why_it_matters: Residents will be asked at special town meeting to vote on the articles the board put on the warrant, including a firefighter pension credit, a motel permit and Marshall Park engineering.
The ARPA requests exceed the money available and carry spending deadlines, so some requests will go unfunded, and the remaining one-time money is not yet allocated.
The higher rate on the renewed note raises the town's borrowing cost for the ladder truck and property purchase, which is paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: October 18: the board votes on all warrant articles and its recommendations, including the motel article.
October 11 or 18: APDC returns with a revised bylaw article, and the board decides its format and whether to include it.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all six votes we captured and on most ARPA dollar figures; the remaining differences are mostly misheard names and digits. The one that matters is that the official minutes record a passed vote releasing executive session minutes that ours omits, and ours records an October 18 deferral the official does not.
